To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sign-changing superconducting state $s_\pm$, which exists in the clean limit, can be destroyed by disorder.
the disorder-induced transition between the sign-changing and the sign-preserving superconducting states is temperature-dependent.
the $s_\mp$ to $s_{++$ transition in the two-band model is temperature- and impurity-dependent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of impurities in the two-band model.
the interplay between the impurity scattering, the temperature, and the superconducting gap structure in Fe-based superconductors.
the temperature-disorder behavior of the superconductivity in iron-based materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the $s_{+}$ state is stable against the non-magnetic impurities, while the $s_{-}$ state is not.
the disorder can drive the $s_\pi$ state towards the $s_{++)}$ state, but not vice versa.

the impurity-induced sign-changing $s_\pm\to s_{++}\to s_\pm$ transition occurs at low temperature for a narrow range of the disorder, but at higher temperature it transforms back into the sign-changing $s_{\rm \pm}$ state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the $s_\mp$ state is stable against the disorder for low enough impurity concentrations.
the $s_\mp$ state with the two sign-changing gaps is the most robust state against the disorder.
the temperature-disorder dependence of the superconductive gaps is crucial for the understanding of the disorder-induced $T_c$ suppression and its relation to the sign change of the gaps.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the $s_{+} \to s_\pm \to \to s_{+} +$ transition is a generic feature of the two-band superconductivity with impurities.
the temperature-dependent $s_{\rm \pm}\to s_{\rm ++}$ transitions can explain the experimental observations of the sign-reversal of the superconductivity in iron-based materials.
the $s_\mp \to s_{+}$ transitions in the multiband model are not always accompanied by the sign-preserving gap.
